newsitem.title: MOROCCO: French Lyonnaise sees Morocco deal as test.
newsitem.headline: French Lyonnaise sees Morocco deal as test.

text.p: The French firm Lyonnaise des Eaux, trying to ward off criticism from local businessmen, said on Tuesday a 35 billion dirhams ($3.8 billion) deal with Morocco would be a test for the North African country to lure foreign investors.
"If the accord fails, it would be a terrible blow for foreign investment in Morocco," said Gilbert During, the French firm's liaison office head in Casablanca.
He dismissed assertions by local businessmen that his firm's takeover of the water and power distribution networks in Casablanca would send energy prices up and hinder local industry competitivness.
"There are 3.5 million people who will benefit from the investment," During told Reuters.
Lyonnaise des Eaux is widely expected to sign soon with the local authority a multibillion dollar investment deal spread over 30 years in Morocco's financial centre of Casablanca.
The French firm, in a 30-year concession accord, will upgrade the city's water and electricity networks.

Lyonnaise des Eaux has however come under fire from the Moroccan opposition and local industrialists over "expected increased water and electricity costs once the concession has been granted to the French firm," a market analyst said.
Casablanca city council has been negotiating since last year with the French firm for it to take over management of the city water, electricity and public waste systems from 1997 to 2027.

The Casablanca-based businessmen's group, Confederation Generale des Entreprises du Maroc, has criticised the planned concession. It said a "review of the draft deal shows a strong prospects of increased bills".
This will particularly hit industry which the confederation says consumes nearly half of the energy distributed in Casablanca.
